name: Programme Change Trigger
respondentAction: Show what actually triggers curriculum/programme change.

name: Future Graduate Outcome Map
respondentAction: Map selected future capabilities to intended/developed/demonstrated/assessed locations.

name: Programme Obsolescence Scenario
respondentAction: Test what happens when a core task/content area becomes less valuable due to AI.

name: Agility & External Validation
respondentAction: Assess review cycle, approval speed and external input.

name: Programme Reality Sample
respondentAction: Inspect representative programmes for actual implementation and transfer.

name: Faculty Practice Reality
respondentAction: Capture where faculty actually use AI and for what academic purpose.

name: Training-to-Practice Conversion
respondentAction: Measure whether faculty development changes practice rather than attendance only.

name: Teaching Redesign Scenario
respondentAction: Test faculty response when AI can perform a taught task.

name: Academic Workforce Change
respondentAction: Assess role/workflow changes, support and leadership response.

name: Faculty Capability Sample
respondentAction: Triangulate claims through teaching/research artefacts and support mechanisms.

name: Student AI Capability Reality
respondentAction: Identify what students can actually do with AI, not merely whether they use it.

name: Agency & Intellectual Independence
respondentAction: Test whether students retain responsibility for questions, reasoning and decisions.

name: Transfer & Practical Capability
respondentAction: Assess application to unfamiliar/real-world situations.

name: Future Transition Readiness
respondentAction: Assess career adaptability, portfolios, employer exposure and creator capability.

name: Equity & Student Voice
respondentAction: Assess unequal access and whether student feedback changes institutional action.

name: Assessment Reality Test
respondentAction: Across representative programmes, what do students actually have to demonstrate to complete major assessments?

name: AI Substitution Test
respondentAction: If generative AI could produce a plausible answer to a major assessment today, what would still make the assessment academically meaningful?

name: Capability Proof Test
respondentAction: How does the institution know that students possess the capabilities its programmes say they develop?

name: Unfamiliar Problem Test
respondentAction: How often are students asked to solve unfamiliar or ambiguous problems where there is no prepared model answer?

name: Assessment Learning Loop
respondentAction: When assessment evidence shows students are weak in an important capability, what normally happens?

name: Data Reality Test
respondentAction: If leadership needs a reliable answer about students, programmes, faculty, placements or research today, how quickly can the institution produce it?

name: Data Journey Test
respondentAction: What normally happens to an important institutional data point from its creation to its use in a decision?

name: AI Infrastructure Test
respondentAction: Which institutional capabilities are currently sufficient to support responsible AI-enabled academic or administrative use?

name: Decision Intelligence Test
respondentAction: Give one recent leadership decision where institutional data or analytics materially changed the decision.

name: Employer Signal Test
respondentAction: How does the institution identify what employers and professional sectors will expect from graduates over the next 3–5 years?

name: Capability-to-Career Test
respondentAction: For a representative programme, how clearly can the institution connect intended graduate capabilities to actual occupational or professional requirements?

name: AI Work Redesign Test
respondentAction: Where AI is changing entry-level work in a major sector relevant to the institution, what has the institution changed for students?

name: Recruiter Confidence Test
respondentAction: What evidence does the institution use to determine whether recruiters trust the capabilities of its graduates?

name: Research Direction Test
respondentAction: What research questions or themes does the institution believe will matter most to its disciplines, region or society over the next 5–10 years?

name: Research-to-Value Test
respondentAction: Take one significant research activity. What happened after the research generated a meaningful finding?

name: Interdisciplinary Collision Test
respondentAction: When a major problem crosses disciplinary boundaries, how does the institution bring the required expertise together?

name: AI Research Judgement Test
respondentAction: Where AI is used in research, how does the institution protect research quality, provenance, integrity and human judgement?

name: Student Creator Test
respondentAction: How are students enabled to move from consuming existing knowledge to creating new knowledge, prototypes, evidence or solutions?

name: Change-to-Action Test
respondentAction: When a development could materially affect the institution, what normally happens between first awareness and an institutional response?

name: Resource Reallocation Test
respondentAction: If leadership decides that an emerging capability has become strategically important, how can resources actually be redirected?

name: Failure Learning Test
respondentAction: When an important institutional experiment does not work, what usually happens?

name: Future Shock Test
respondentAction: Imagine that within five years AI materially changes 20–30% of entry-level tasks across several major sectors relevant to your institution. Which five institutional responses would leadership prioritise first?

name: Adaptation Reality Test
respondentAction: Which statement best describes the institution today?
